sections.name: Boo
sections.card:
Summary: A ghost found on every board that robs another player of coins or a Star. The Boo Bell item calls one up whenever you want, and a Boo can also serve as a Duel Mode partner.
Weak points: If you hold a Boo Repellant, a Boo that tries to rob you of coins or a Star sets it off automatically and runs away empty-handed. As a duel partner, a Boo that gets attacked hits back with the same amount of damage before vanishing, but it does not strike back at a Thwomp, and strikes back at a Chain Chomp only when it stands directly in front.
Tips: On Waluigi's Island a Boo gives you a choice of two paths instead, though one is rigged and returns you to the start. When you ring a Boo up with the Boo Bell, he asks who the target is and what to take. In Duel Mode, Yoshi begins with a Boo as his partner.

sections.name: Bowser and the Bowser Space
sections.card:
Summary: When you land on a Bowser Space, Bowser shows up. Most often he goes after your coins, but he may also give out items or put a curse on all the players.
Weak points: In Mario Party 3 the roulette is not left to chance. It stops on whatever event the pointer is over at the moment you press the button, so careful timing lets you choose. A player with no coins is spared: Bowser pays you instead, 30 coins, or 40 or 50 depending on where you rank, no event takes place and no Stars are lost.
Looks like: Bowser flashes a color when an event starts: purple for Bowser's Curse, green for Bowser's Reverse Curse, yellow for Bowser Shuffle and red for Bowser Revolution.
Tips: Bowser's Curse forces all four players, on their following turn, to move just 1 to 3 spaces, as a Poison Mushroom would. Bowser's Reverse Curse sends them backwards instead, as a Reverse Mushroom would. Either curse can be cancelled by an item that counters it. Bowser Shuffle mixes up where the four players stand, and he can also give you a free Bowser Phone (very rarely two) or a free Bowser Suit.

sections.name: Game Guy and the Game Guy Space
sections.card:
Summary: A game-show host who takes all your coins when you land on his space, then runs a luck-based minigame in which you either get them back doubled (or more) or lose them all. Game Guy Spaces turn up in both Party Mode and Duel Mode.
Weak points: His four minigames are Game Guy's Lucky 7, Magic Boxes, Roulette and Sweet Surprise, and they depend mostly on luck. A typical result is that you double your coins or lose the lot, although you can gamble for bigger multiples.
Looks like: A Shy Guy with a yellowish mask and a bowtie.
Tips: The Lucky Charm item sends a chosen player, even yourself, to a Game Guy minigame without landing on his space. In Game Guy's Room you can practise: you start with 10 coins, may bet up to 100, and aim to reach 1,000, and winning earns you Mario's Puzzle Party Pro, a rare minigame. The room itself only opens once Story Mode has been finished with eight or more S rankings.

sections.name: Evil Woody
sections.card:
Summary: Woody's unfriendly twin on the Woody Woods board. Stop on a Happening Space by Evil Woody and you must take one of two costly fruits: a Reverse Block Fruit (you roll, but move backwards) or a Minus Coin Fruit (you lose five coins).
Weak points: You choose one of the two fruits yourself, but if you pick neither Evil Woody always gives you the Reverse Block Fruit, so the only way to avoid the backwards move is to choose the Minus Coin Fruit.
Looks like: A tree whose color palette is the inverse of Woody's, blue with purple leaves, with a perpetually angry expression.
Tips: Three ? Spaces ring Evil Woody. The friendly Woody on the same board offers good fruits instead: a Plus Block Fruit that gives a second dice roll, or a Plus Coin Fruit worth five coins. If you choose neither, he gives you the extra Dice Block.

sections.name: Deep Bloober Sea's torpedo and anglerfish traps
sections.card:
Summary: Creatures in Deep Bloober Sea can shift you across the board: a Sushi in a submarine can fire you onto the other path, a giant vacuum anglerfish can pull you in and spit you out again, and a giant Blooper Baby calls for its mother, whose tentacle carries you over to the far side.
Weak points: At the submarine junction you press one of four buttons: three are harmless and one sends a torpedo that knocks you onto the opposite path. The button layout stays fixed until someone presses the wrong one, and now and then the Sushi simply does not see you and lets you through. Against the anglerfish, keep tapping the button to struggle against the pull, or it swallows you.
Looks like: A Sushi (a shark) in a submarine looking over the main junction, a giant vacuum anglerfish with an arrow on it that spins, and a giant Blooper Baby.
Tips: The anglerfish's spinning arrow settles pointing down, to the front or to the right. A player it swallows ends up close to a Sushi, close to Boo, or at the starting point. The board has 93 spaces in all, 5 of them Bowser Spaces and 2 Game Guy Spaces.

sections.name: Waluigi's Island's dynamite and rigged path
sections.card:
Summary: An unlockable board full of traps. Every landing on a Happening Space on the dynamite island lowers a counter that begins at 5; at 0 the dynamite goes off, and every player caught in the blast forfeits all their coins.
Weak points: To leave the dynamite island you hit the gear at the middle of the board in the Action Time. Whichever arrow is lit as you land shows the path you have to follow; if it stops on the down arrow, or you act too slowly, you are stuck on the island. On the road to Boo there are two paths, and one is booby-trapped and returns you to the start.
Looks like: An island of dynamite with a counter in the middle of the explosives that begins at five, and a gear at the board's center with four arrows that light up one after another, clockwise.
Tips: On the dynamite island the Happening Spaces are the ones to fear. On the island in the upper left every space turns into a different type each turn, apart from the Bank Space, and on the upper sides of the board the red pipes always carry you to the green pipe by the start.

sections.name: Chain Chomp (duel partner)
sections.card:
Summary: A chainless Chain Chomp that can be a Duel Mode partner; its attack hits the opponent and all their partners at once. Its attack is 1, its stamina 2 and its salary six coins.
Weak points: A Boo partner counterattacks against a Chain Chomp's multi-hit only when it stands right in front of that Chain Chomp.
Looks like: Chain Chomps are black or dark blue balls with large round eyes and a wide open mouth full of razor-sharp teeth; the Duel Mode partner comes without a chain.
Tips: No character begins with a Chain Chomp; you win one from the partner lottery. A powered-up Chain Chomp swells to Shark Chomp size, leaps and slams down on every opponent. Pairing a Bob-omb with a Chomp makes the Millennium Star comment on the pair, but the attack is not raised.

sections.name: Thwomp (duel partner)
sections.card:
Summary: A Duel Mode partner whose attack is 0, yet it flattens any of the enemy's partners in one go and leaves the enemy player untouched. It has 2 stamina and a salary of four coins.
Weak points: Used against you, it takes out your partners in one hit and does nothing to you, the player. A Boo partner that a Thwomp defeats does not hit back as it normally would.
Looks like: A blue, cube-shaped block of stone with the up-to-date Thwomp face on it; the colour and the shape are the original ones.
Tips: No character begins with a Thwomp, so one can only turn up through the partner roulette. With two Thwomps, the Millennium Star reduces their salaries by one rather than raising their attack, and it also remarks on a Whomp and Thwomp pairing. The instruction booklet states an attack of 2 by mistake.

sections.name: Boo Repellant
sections.card:
Summary: A spray can that makes Boo flee without stealing from you. Toad sells it for 10 coins, and the manual spells it Boo Repellent.
Uses: While you hold it, it sets itself off the moment Boo moves to take your coins or a Star, and Boo runs off with nothing. A can can be used only once.
Tips: At the start of your turn you may discard one to free up space, and that counts as your item use for the turn. Other players are put off trying a Boo steal on you, so its effect often lasts a long time, but computer players ignore it and go ahead regardless, Stars included.

sections.name: Boo Bell
sections.card:
Summary: Rings up Boo to steal coins or a Star from an opponent. Baby Bowser sells it for 15 coins.
Uses: Using it calls up Boo, who asks you to name the victim and the loot. From the target he takes either coins or a Star.
Tips: Anyone carrying a Boo Repellant sends Boo away and loses nothing. Baby Bowser's shop, which mainly sells items for hindering opponents, is where the Boo Bell is sold.

sections.name: Plunder Chest
sections.card:
Summary: A treasure chest that takes an item from an opponent of your choosing. Only Baby Bowser's shop sells it, for 10 coins, and Princess Peach likes it best of all items.
Uses: You choose the opponent to rob; if they hold several items, which one is taken is left to chance. You cannot use the loot until after you have rolled.
Tips: The Barter Box is similar, but the Plunder Chest takes just one item, whereas the Barter Box trades over all of them. When Peach is computer-controlled she goes for it ahead of other items if she can.

sections.name: Lucky Lamp
sections.card:
Summary: A lamp that holds Mushroom Jeanie, who moves the Star to a different space. Baby Bowser's shop sells it for 10 coins, and it is the counterpart of the Magic Lamp.
Uses: Mushroom Jeanie appears at the Star Space when it is used and relocates the Star elsewhere on the board, rather than carrying you to it as the Magic Lamp does.
Tips: On Spiny Desert, which has a mirage Millennium Star, she always heads for the real one. Baby Bowser's shop sells the Lucky Lamp, and an item minigame can award it too.

sections.name: Bowser Phone
sections.card:
Summary: Rings Bowser up so that he runs one of his events on a player of your choice, just as if that player had stepped on a Bowser Space. It is sold at Baby Bowser's shop for 10 coins.
Uses: You pick an opponent, or yourself, to be on the receiving end of one of Bowser's events, and you may look over the board first. There is also an option that leaves the choice to Bowser, who then picks a random player.
Tips: The player you choose really does go to see Bowser, at the castle spot the Bowser Space uses. You can also be given a Bowser Phone free of charge by a Bowser Space.

sections.name: Lucky Charm
sections.card:
Summary: A rare coin bearing Game Guy's picture on one side. Using it makes a chosen player stake all their coins on a Game Guy minigame. Neither shop sells it.
Uses: Using it calls Game Guy, who collects every one of the target's coins and starts a Game Guy minigame. The target may be another player or yourself.
Tips: Toad can hand you one when you land on an Item Space, a hidden block rarely holds one, and so can an Item Bag bought at Baby Bowser's Joint.

sections.name: Wacky Watch
sections.card:
Summary: A rare item that moves the game straight to five turns from the finish. No Item Shop sells it.
Uses: Using it sets the game to the point where five turns are left, so it can cut a game very short, or stretch it out if used when fewer than five turns remain.
Tips: Toad can give you one on an Item Space, and a Hidden Block can hold one too. It is unique among this game's items in never being sold in a shop or found in an Item Bag. If you use it on what would have been the last turn, the remainder of that turn still counts as the last, so the Item Shops stay shut.
